solutions.check: bars rebuilt from the blog's numbered answers (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Good fitter chucking out British Gas reducer

indicators.note: to chuck out is to throw away, so the British letter is removed from the comparative

blocks.note: G is the standard abbreviation for good
fitter, in health terms, is better
B is the abbreviation for British

explanation.surface: A competent plumber turns out to be a British Gas fitter who reduces gas.
explanation.walkthrough: GETTER is G plus BETTER without its B. 'British Gas' looks like the utility company, but British is the letter to drop and Gas belongs to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A getter is a substance put inside a vacuum tube to absorb the remaining traces of gas.

clue.text: Zip about with cunning in Grammar School racers

indicators.note: in places these letters within the school's initials

blocks.note: zip is nothing, zero, the letter O
c is short for circa, about
art means craft or cunning
GS is the abbreviation for grammar school

explanation.surface: Pupils at a grammar school cleverly zoom about in their racing cars.
explanation.walkthrough: O, C and ART go inside G...S.
explanation.definitionFit: Go-carts, or karts, are small low motor vehicles raced on tracks.

clue.text: One article in ten is to do with the poet Anacreon

definitions.text: to do with the poet Anacreon

indicators.note: in places the first two pieces within the number

blocks.note: Roman numeral one
the indefinite article
taken as written

explanation.surface: One article in ten concerns an ancient Greek poet.
explanation.definitionFit: Anacreon came from Teos, an Ionian city, so anything relating to him or his home is Teian.

clue.text: Sort of cross about bloke's very tall tree

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the cross is wrapped around the man

blocks.note: a tau cross is T-shaped
a bloke is a man; the 's reads as 'is' joining to the definition

explanation.surface: An angry man is about to fell an enormous tree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cross' looks like angry; it is the T-shaped tau cross. Bloke is British slang for a man.
explanation.definitionFit: The tamanu is a large tropical timber tree of the Pacific, prized for its oil and its height.

clue.text: We got up around noon, finally time to dive in?

indicators.note: in a down clue, getting up means rising from the bottom, so the word reads upwards
finally points to the last letter of each word it governs
around means surrounding, so the pronoun wraps the selected letters

blocks.note: taken as written
last letter of noon
last letter of time

explanation.surface: We rose at midday, and at last it was time for a swim.
explanation.walkthrough: WE reversed is EW, wrapping the last letters of noon and time.
explanation.definitionFit: Enew is a Spenserian falconry word for driving a bird to plunge into water, hence diving in.

clue.text: Costermonger beginning to peddle with the larks?

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its opening letter, so only that is kept

blocks.note: first letter of peddle
up with the larks means up early

explanation.surface: A street trader starts selling at dawn.
explanation.walkthrough: A costermonger is a London street seller of fruit and vegetables; pearlies are costermongers who wear pearl-button suits.
explanation.definitionFit: In Chambers a pearly is a costermonger, from the pearl-button costumes of London's street-trader royalty.

clue.text: Where baby sits up with posh Australian living near Slough?

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means read from the bottom, so the word for where a baby sits runs upward

blocks.note: a baby sits on a lap
U means upper-class
Strine is Australian English as spoken

explanation.surface: Where does the baby of a well-off Australian sit, living near Slough?
explanation.walkthrough: Slough is an English town near London; here a slough is a bog. LAP reversed is PAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Palustrine means marshy or living in marshes, and a slough is a swamp or bog.

clue.text: "Bewitched" personality skipping opening spell

indicators.note: skipping the opening means jumping past the first letter, so it is lost

blocks.note: the self is one's personality
a shot is a go, a spell at something

explanation.surface: A bewitched character is missing the first part of a magic spell.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spell' points at magic beside bewitched, but here it means a turn or attempt.
explanation.definitionFit: Elfshot means struck by an elf's arrow, so afflicted by sorcery, i.e. under enchantment.

clue.text: Mostly travelling funfair attraction, but deserted, is noisy in Nairn

indicators.note: mostly means not quite all, so the last letter goes
deserted is abbreviated d in Chambers, and here that letter has left the attraction

blocks.note: on the road means travelling
a ride at a fair

explanation.surface: A travelling fair's ride stands empty but is still loud.
explanation.walkthrough: ROAD loses its last letter; RIDE loses D, the abbreviation for deserted. Nairn is a Scottish town, flagging a Scots word.
explanation.definitionFit: Roarie is Scots for roaring or noisy, hence a word one might hear in a Scottish town.

clue.text: State of sensational staginess as snide slur gets snarled

indicators.note: something snarled is tangled up, so its letters are knotted into a new order

blocks.note: the fodder, nine letters

explanation.surface: A melodramatic scene unfolds as a nasty insult is growled.
explanation.definitionFit: Lurid means shocking and sensational, so luridness is the quality of being melodramatically vivid.

clue.text: Hostel exploits first date released for proceeds of old poetry

indicators.note: releasing the first date lets the opening d go, so it drops out

blocks.note: the Y is the YMCA or YWCA hostel
exploits are deeds

explanation.surface: A youth hostel's heroic exploits, first published, earn money for old verse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Proceeds' looks like income; it is the verb, goes. D is the abbreviation for date.
explanation.definitionFit: Yeed is an archaic Spenserian verb meaning to go, so yeeds means goes or proceeds in old verse.

clue.text: Lad on lane unsettling every Tom, Dick, and Harry

indicators.note: unsettling something disturbs it, so the words before are rearranged

blocks.note: the fodder, nine letters

explanation.surface: A boy on a country lane is disturbing all the passers-by.
explanation.definitionFit: Every Tom, Dick and Harry is an idiom for everybody, just as one and all means everyone.

clue.text: Fancy forgetting a tabard

indicators.note: forgetting something leaves it out, so the article is dropped

blocks.note: a chimera is a fanciful notion
the letter to drop

explanation.surface: A fancy-dress outfit has been made without its tabard.
explanation.walkthrough: CHIMERA minus A leaves CHIMER, a variant of chimere, the bishop's sleeveless robe.
explanation.definitionFit: A chimer is a loose sleeveless upper robe, close in form to a tabard, a sleeveless tunic.

clue.text: Malign program managed conflict amongst a few

indicators.note: amongst means placed among, so the conflict goes within the few

blocks.note: to run something is to manage it
some means a few
war is conflict

explanation.surface: A wicked scheme stirred up conflict among a small group.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Malign' reads as a verb, to slander, but here it is an adjective meaning harmful.
explanation.definitionFit: Ransomware is malicious software that locks a victim's files until a ransom is paid.

clue.text: Passengers left inside spread out

indicators.note: inside places one thing within another, so the letter goes into the word for passengers

blocks.note: a taxi's fare is its passenger, used collectively
L is the abbreviation for left

explanation.surface: Passengers left inside a vehicle spread out across the seats.
explanation.definitionFit: To flare is to widen out, as a skirt or nostrils spread outward.

clue.text: Ban rash soaring with, eg, eagles

indicators.note: soaring wheels and swoops around, so the letters are sent into a new arrangement

blocks.note: fodder, seven letters
taken as written

explanation.surface: Outlaw rash flying with birds such as eagles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'eg, eagles' looks like an example; eg is fodder and eagles is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Berghaan is Afrikaans for mountain cock, the South African name for the bateleur and similar eagles.

clue.text: Profit by free means of access

blocks.note: to use a thing is to profit by it
to free is to rid

explanation.surface: Take advantage of free entry.
explanation.definitionFit: A user ID is the login name that gives a person access to a computer system.

clue.text: Backsliding offender bagging new agents of clottiness?

indicators.note: sliding back means going in the opposite direction, so the word reads right to left
to bag something is to put it in a bag, so the word holds the letter

blocks.note: a sinner is an offender
N is the abbreviation for new

explanation.surface: A repeat offender carries off the new agents of some stupid scheme.
explanation.walkthrough: SINNER reversed is RENNIS, which takes N inside. The question mark flags 'clottiness' as clotting, not stupidity.
explanation.definitionFit: Rennin is the enzyme that curdles milk, so rennins are agents that make it clot.

clue.text: See one on dual screen? The answer is more than one

definitions.text: The answer is more than one

blocks.note: V stands for vide, Latin for see
Roman numeral one
the Nintendo DS games console takes its name from dual screen

explanation.surface: Watch something on a split screen and the answer is a plural.
explanation.walkthrough: The first sentence also describes a video watched on a screen; the second sentence says the answer is the plural, short video clips.
explanation.definitionFit: Vids are video recordings; the definition only asks for a plural of something seen on screen, which the first sentence supplies.

clue.text: On tour test progressive rock

indicators.note: progressive rock shifts and develops, so the letters move into a new order

blocks.note: the fodder, ten letters

explanation.surface: A band on tour tests out its progressive rock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Progressive rock' reads as a music genre, but progressive is the anagram signal and rock alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Troutstone is a speckled igneous rock, a variety of troctolite named for its trout-like spots.

clue.text: NZ settlement to cut that which enlightens chap in charge

indicators.note: cutting into something means entering it, so the settlement goes inside

blocks.note: a torch gives light
a pa is a fortified Maori village in New Zealand

explanation.surface: A New Zealand village cuts into the lamp of a man who leads.
explanation.definitionFit: A toparch is the ruler of a small district or state, so a local governor.

clue.text: Conveniences exist near trotters

blocks.note: to be is to exist
trotters are pigs' feet, hoofs

explanation.surface: Toilets are located close to the pig pens.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Conveniences' suggests lavatories, a British euphemism; here it means benefits.
explanation.definitionFit: Behoof means advantage or benefit, so behoofs are things done for one's convenience.

clue.text: A few without getting into legal wrong here, possibly

indicators.note: getting into something means entering it, so the abbreviation goes inside the legal wrong
possibly suggests one of several arrangements, so the word before is rearranged

blocks.note: w/o is the short form of without
a tort is a civil wrong in law
the anagram fodder

explanation.surface: A few people might commit a legal wrong here without meaning to.
explanation.walkthrough: W/O is the shorthand for without used on forms; a tort is a civil wrong such as negligence, rather than a crime.
explanation.definitionFit: Two or three is an everyday phrase for a small number, which is what a few means.

clue.text: One keen on flip-flops edges from lefty in snappish manner?

indicators.note: the edges of a word are its outermost letters, so only those are kept

blocks.note: a tart, taken as one who flips from partner to partner
outer letters of lefty

explanation.surface: A beach-sandal fan picks at a left-winger in a sharp manner.
explanation.walkthrough: This parse is the best fit found: TART for the cryptic description and the outer letters of lefty, giving TART-LY.
explanation.definitionFit: Tart means sharp or cutting in speech, so speaking tartly is answering snappishly.

clue.text: Personnel dept picked up one about van's first smash in Kyiv

indicators.note: first means only the opening letter of van's is taken
about means surrounding, so the word for one goes round the letter
in a down clue, picked up means lifted, so the letters read from bottom to top

blocks.note: HR, human resources, is the personnel department
any one, any
first letter of van

explanation.surface: HR raises the alarm over a van crash in Ukraine's capital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Smash' looks like the crash; it is slang for loose change, money. Kyiv is the capital of Ukraine.
explanation.definitionFit: The hryvna is the currency of Ukraine, so it is the money, or smash, spent in Kyiv.

clue.text: Pretend to be quiet in the morning

blocks.note: sh is a call for quiet
am means ante meridiem, before noon

explanation.surface: Pretending to be quiet in the early hours so as not to wake anyone.
explanation.definitionFit: To sham is to feign or fake, a synonym for pretend.

clue.text: Society in Gretna greet sausage-loving hound?

blocks.note: S is the abbreviation for society
greet is Scots for weep, and Gretna Green is a Scottish border village

explanation.surface: Society weddings at Gretna Green bring tears, with a dog that loves sausages.
explanation.walkthrough: Gretna Green is the Scottish village famed for runaway weddings. Sweep is the grey dog glove puppet from the British children's show Sooty, who loves sausages.
explanation.definitionFit: Sweep, the squeaky puppet dog in Sooty, is famous for his fondness for sausages.

clue.text: Part-way through ill-considered biblical exegesis

blocks.note: mid means in the middle of
rash means hasty and ill-considered

explanation.surface: Halfway through, a hasty reading of scripture.
explanation.definitionFit: A midrash is a rabbinic commentary interpreting the Hebrew Bible, so it is a form of scriptural interpretation.

clue.text: Actively start to attack erstwhile leader of the House

indicators.note: the start of a word is its opening letter, so only that is kept

blocks.note: first letter of attack
Michael Foot was Labour Leader of the House of Commons in the 1970s

explanation.surface: A former Commons leader is busy beginning an attack.
explanation.definitionFit: Afoot means astir and in progress, so going on actively.

clue.text: City used to be verdant, looking from the east

indicators.note: in an across clue, looking from the east means reading from right to left

blocks.note: was is the past of to be
raw can mean green, inexperienced, as verdant does

explanation.surface: A city once green, seen from the eastern side.
explanation.walkthrough: WAS RAW reversed reads WARSAW.
explanation.definitionFit: Warsaw is the capital city of Poland.

clue.text: A hurdle to get over — Eastern xenophobe banning book

indicators.note: banning something keeps it out, so that letter is removed

blocks.note: the Boxers were the anti-foreign Chinese movement behind the 1900 rising
B is the abbreviation for book

explanation.surface: A foreigner-hating easterner bans a book, an obstacle to overcome.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Eastern' and 'xenophobe' together point at a Boxer of the Chinese rebellion, not E and X.
explanation.definitionFit: An oxer is a fence of hedge and rail, used as a show-jumping obstacle that horses clear.

clue.text: Greengrocer, eg, sells this item which shoots, hard to shift

indicators.note: to shift something is to move it away, so that letter is taken off

blocks.note: heater is slang for a gun
H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils

explanation.surface: A grocer sells a sprouting vegetable that is difficult to move.
explanation.walkthrough: HEATER, gangster slang for a pistol, loses its H. 'Shoots' suggests sprouts, which a greengrocer might sell.
explanation.definitionFit: An eater is an apple or other fruit for eating raw, as opposed to a cooker, sold by greengrocers.

clue.text: Offering direct from Vatican City, surprisingly too

indicators.note: a surprising result is an unexpected arrangement, so the word that follows is mixed up

blocks.note: ex means direct from, as goods ex works
V is Vatican City's international vehicle code
the anagram fodder

explanation.surface: A gift arrives straight from the Vatican, unexpectedly as well.
explanation.definitionFit: An ex voto is a votive offering made in fulfilment of a vow, often hung in a church.

clue.text: Sift loose rock and anger no end

indicators.note: having no end means its closing part has gone, so those letters are cut

blocks.note: scree is loose stones on a mountainside
'n' is a short form of and, as in rock 'n' roll
to offend is to anger

explanation.surface: Sieve the loose stones and stay calm about it.
explanation.walkthrough: OFFEND loses the letters END, which is what 'no end' says literally.
explanation.definitionFit: To screen off is to separate or filter out, which is what sifting does.

clue.text: Blasted hype is full of cold soul

indicators.note: something blasted is blown apart, so the letters are scattered and rearranged
being full of something means holding it, so the letter goes inside

blocks.note: hype is, contracted to hype's
C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps

explanation.surface: Damned publicity has a cold heart.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'is' does double duty: 'hype is' gives HYPES as fodder, while 'full of' places C inside the shuffled letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Psyche is the Greek word for the soul or spirit, still used for the human mind.

clue.text: Renegade detained by soldiers without charge

indicators.note: someone detained by others is held among them, so the word sits inside

blocks.note: GIs are American soldiers
a rat is one who deserts his side

explanation.surface: A traitor held by troops is released without being charged.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without charge' sounds like no criminal charge; here it means free of cost.
explanation.definitionFit: Gratis means free, costing nothing, from the Latin for 'as a favour'.
